newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: CYCLONE THREAT AND CONTINUED FLOODING IN QLD
A cyclone has formed in the Coral Sea off the north Queensland coast, and is continuing to intensify.
The Weather Bureau says Cyclone Justin is about 800 kilometres east of Cairns and 650 kilometres northeast of Mackay, and is moving slowly west.
Meanwhile, flooding around the state is continuing to cut off towns, and force people out of their homes.
Police at Mount Isa in the state's north west say four or five streets in the city were evacuated overnight because of flooding from the Leichhardt River.
There's also flooding at Urandangie and other small towns in the region, and roads are cut to Cloncurry where houses were inundated yesterday.
TALKS URGED ON GRAND PRIX STRIKE
Emergency talks between the Victorian Government and unions are being urged, in a bid to avert this weekend's public transport strike.
The 48-hour stoppage, beginning at midnight tonight, will bring Melbourne's public transport to a standstill, disrupting access to the Formula One Grand Prix.

The Government's indicated it's not prepared to negotiate on its offer of a six per cent pay rise, but the Victorian Trades Hall Council's, Leigh Hubbard, says fresh negotiations today could be productive.
If the strike goes ahead, Melbourne's Bus Proprietors Association says it's prepared to do the job, and has at least 450 buses on standby to get people to and from the track.
COUNTER TERRORISM SKILLS UPGRADED FOR OLYMPICS
The Defence Minister Ian McLachlan says counter terrorism personnel will need more training before the Sydney 2000 Olympics.
But he says the elite counter-terrorism regiment will be ready.
Mr McLachlan's comments come as the Army considers whether to court-martial three officers, following the report on last year's Blackhawk accident near Townsville which killed 18 servicemen.
The Army says it'll take administrative action against two other officers.
The Board of Inquiry found the flight lead helicopter turned into another, and that was the result of a chain of events beforehand.
The Defence Force admits more work is still needed on night-time formation flying of Blackhawks.
FATAL AIR CRASH NEAR KATHERINE
Bureau of Air Safety Investigations examiners are expected to arrive in Katherine today to investigate the fatal crash of a vintage aircraft yesterday.
A 57 year old man from Toowoomba in Queensland died when the World War Two Harvard aircraft he was flying crashed just off the northern end of the Katherine airport runway.
His 49 year old passenger was taken to the Katherine Hospital with head injuries and suspected fractures.
Air North Regional staff member Mario Martinelli says it appeared the wing broke away from the Harvard's fuselage and caught fire as it crashed.
